issues.title: [Bug] StackOverflowError during clean config generation in 26.3.4
issues.body:
### Mod loader

Fabric

### Minecraft version

26.3

### Mod version

26.3.4 [release]

### Modloader version

Fabric 0.19.5

### Modpack info

Nope

### [IMPORTANT] If bug:

- [x] I have confirmed this bug is reproducible on a minimal setup, not a modpack with many other mods.

### [IMPORTANT] If bug: The **latest.log** file, not the crash report

https://p.kdan.dev/7lgHrL9

### Issue description

Description:
Upgrading from 26.3.3-beta with pre-existing configuration files loads normally without issues. However, when starting Jade 26.3.4 with a clean profile or after deleting the Jade configuration folder, the game immediately crashes during startup with java.lang.StackOverflowError. This issue is consistently reproducible in a minimal environment with only Jade 26.3.4 and Fabric API installed.

Steps to Reproduce:
1. Install Jade 26.3.4 on Fabric mc26.3.
2. Delete the 'config/jade' folder or any jade*.json config files.
3. Launch the game.
4. The game crashes during plugin initialization.

Root Cause Analysis:
During fresh configuration creation, WailaConfig.fixData() calls ClientPluginConfig.ensureEntry(), which fires notifyChange(). The CorePlugin change listener then immediately invokes IWailaConfig.get() before initialization is finalized, causing JsonConfig$CachedSupplier to re-invoke WailaConfig.fixData() in an infinite re-entrant recursive loop.


Minecraft crashed without a crash report. The logs have been uploaded to `paste.kostromdan.dev`:
### [latest.log](<https://p.kdan.dev/7lgHrL9>)   |   [crash_assistant_app.log](<https://p.kdan.dev/sDDso4M>)   |   [modlist.txt](<https://p.kdan.dev/KwdbSVI>)

issues.title: Crash when biome added via runtime mixin (Unreferenced key in registry validation)
issues.body:
### Mod loader

NeoForge

### Minecraft version

26.1.2

### Mod version

26.1.10

### Modloader version

Neoforge 26.1.2.95

### Modpack info

 Just Jade + a biome mod that adds biomes via runtime SourceProvider mixin

### [IMPORTANT] If bug:

- [x] I have confirmed this bug is reproducible on a minimal setup, not a modpack with many other mods.

### [IMPORTANT] If bug: The **latest.log** file, not the crash report

_No response_

### Issue description

Jade's registerTagsUpdatedListener calls VanillaRegistries.createLookup() which triggers static registry validation. This crashes the game with Unreferenced key when a mod adds biomes to a MultiNoiseBiomeSourceParameterList via a runtime mixin (wrapping the SourceProvider) instead of a static biome source JSON. The biomes exist and generate correctly, but the static validator doesn't see them as referenced because they're only added when apply() is called at worldgen time.

The createLookup() call should either be wrapped in a try/catch or use a different method that doesn't enforce the "all biomes must be statically referenced" check.

issues.title: NullPointerException in isAcceptableEntity when entity is null during clearLevel
issues.body:
### Mod loader

Fabric

### Minecraft version

26.1.2

### Mod version

26.1.8

### Modloader version

Fabric: Loader 0.19.3 + API 0.149.1

### Modpack info

_No response_

### [IMPORTANT] If bug:

- [ ] I have confirmed this bug is reproducible on a minimal setup, not a modpack with many other mods.

### [IMPORTANT] If bug: The **latest.log** file, not the crash report

_No response_

### Issue description

When switching servers (e.g., proxy sub-server transfer), `ClientPacketListener.clearLevel()` triggers `ClientEntityEvents.ENTITY_UNLOAD` for all entities in the level. Some entities may resolve to `null` during this process, causing a `NullPointerException` at `DatapackBlockManager.isAcceptableEntity()`.
This bug also exists in the latest version.
Stack trace:
```
java.lang.NullPointerException: Cannot invoke "net.minecraft.world.entity.Entity.getType()" because "entity" is null
    at snownee.jade.overlay.DatapackBlockManager.isAcceptableEntity(DatapackBlockManager.java:102)
    at snownee.jade.overlay.DatapackBlockManager.onEntityLeave(DatapackBlockManager.java:38)
    at snownee.jade.util.ClientProxy.onEntityLeave(ClientProxy.java:134)
    at net.fabricmc.fabric.api.client.event.lifecycle.v1.ClientEntityEvents.lambda$static$3(ClientEntityEvents.java:47)
    at net.minecraft.client.multiplayer.ClientPacketListener.clearLevel(ClientPacketListener.java)
```
Proposed fix: Add a null guard in `isAcceptableEntity`:
```java
public static boolean isAcceptableEntity(Entity entity) {
    if (entity == null) return false;
    return entity.getType() == EntityType.BLOCK_DISPLAY || entity.getType() == EntityType.ITEM_DISPLAY;
}
```
Steps to reproduce:
1.Join a Velocity/BungeeCord proxy network with multiple backend servers
2.Switch between servers (triggering `clearLevel`)
3.Crash occurs when a mod creates client-side entities (e.g., nametag/bubble displays) that get caught in the entity unload event

issues.title: [26.2 Fabric] Fractional horse health renders half a heart lower than the vanilla mount HUD
issues.body:
### Mod loader

Fabric

### Minecraft version

26.2

### Mod version

26.2.9+fabric

### Modloader version

Fabric Loader 0.19.3 + Fabric API 0.155.0+26.2

### Modpack info

Custom client instance. The server is vanilla 26.2.

### [IMPORTANT] If bug:

- [ ] I have confirmed this bug is reproducible on a minimal setup, not a modpack with many other mods.

### [IMPORTANT] If bug: The **latest.log** file, not the crash report

No crash or relevant log error is produced. This is a deterministic rendering/rounding issue.

### Issue description

A full-health horse with a fractional `minecraft:max_health` value can show one half-heart less in Jade than in Minecraft's vanilla mount HUD.

Example entity data read from the server save:

```text
Health:           27.98603630065918
max_health base:  27.986036147665843
```

The tiny difference is float serialization noise; the horse is at full health.

#### Steps to reproduce

1. Use a full-health horse with fractional max health between 27 and 28 (breeding in 26.2 commonly produces fractional values). The values above reproduce the calculation exactly.
2. Look at the horse with Jade enabled.
3. Jade renders 14 heart containers, but only 13.5 filled hearts.
4. Mount the same horse. The vanilla vehicle HUD renders 14 full hearts.

#### Cause

Jade 26.2's `HealthElement#extractRenderState` starts with:

```java
float health = this.health * 0.5F;
```

It then uses `floor(curHealth)` for full hearts and draws a half heart for the remaining fraction. For the example:

```text
27.986036 / 2 = 13.993018
```

Therefore Jade renders 13 full + 1 half heart.

Minecraft 26.2's vanilla `Hud#extractVehicleHealth`, however, first evaluates:

```java
int health = (int) Math.ceil(vehicle.getHealth());
```

So the same value becomes 28 health points and renders as 14 full hearts. Vanilla also calculates vehicle max-heart slots in `getVehicleMaxHearts` using `(int) (maxHealth + 0.5F) / 2`.

I also checked 44 saved horses from the same stable. 42 had fractional values for which Jade's visible-heart result differs from the vanilla vehicle HUD calculation, so this is not limited to floating-point noise near exactly 28.

#### Expected behavior

For horses/vehicle-health entities, Jade should use the same health normalization as the vanilla mount HUD, so looking at a horse and mounting it do not report different visible health.

A narrowly scoped fix could normalize `getHealth()`/`getMaxHealth()` for `AbstractHorse` in `EntityHealthAndArmorProvider.Client` before constructing `HealthElement`, while retaining the existing generic fractional-health behavior for other entities.

Relevant Jade source:
https://github.com/Snownee/Jade/blob/26.2-fabric/src/main/java/snownee/jade/impl/ui/HealthElement.java#L61-L124

issues.body:
### Mod loader

NeoForge

### Minecraft version

26.1.2

### Mod version

26.0.10+neoforge

### Modloader version

26.1.2.43-beta

### Modpack info

_No response_

### [IMPORTANT] If bug:

- [x] I have confirmed this bug is reproducible on a minimal setup, not a modpack with many other mods.

### [IMPORTANT] If bug: The **latest.log** file, not the crash report

https://gist.github.com/Lolothepro/f9953cbf284d2351129b66300b78ed1c

### Issue description

When EvilCraft is loaded with Jade, an error occurs

In `CommonProxy.loadEntrypoints()`, Jade iterates over every `ModContainer` returned by `ModList.get().getSortedMods()` and calls `getAnnotatedBy(WailaPlugin.class)` on each container's `ScanResult`. When a single JAR declares multiple mods in one `neoforge.mods.toml`, NeoForge creates one `ModContainer` per declared mod, all sharing the same underlying `IModFileInfo` and therefore the same `ScanResult`. This means `getAnnotatedBy()` is called once per `ModContainer`, returning the same `@WailaPlugin` classes each time and adding them multiple times to the `entrypoints` list. Later in `loadPlugins()`, Jade iterates over that list and maintains a `Set<String>` of seen class names, when it encounters a class name already in the set, it calls `throwError("Duplicate plugin class")` instead of skipping it, making the error fatal. The fix should be applied in `loadEntrypoints()` by tracking already-visited `IModFileInfo` instances and skipping any `ModContainer` whose owning file has already been scanned. Alternatively, the fix could be applied in `loadPlugins()` by replacing `throwError()` with a simple `continue` and a warning log when a duplicate class name is detected. Both approaches would make Jade tolerant of the legitimate and long-standing pattern of bundling multiple mods inside a single JAR file.

Code causing the bug:
https://github.com/Snownee/Jade/blob/26.1-neoforge/src/main/java/snownee/jade/util/CommonProxy.java#L392-L406

issues.title: Jade crash on shader toggle / player respawn – ImmutableMultimap.put UnsupportedOperationException (Fabric 1.21.1)
issues.body:
### Mod loader

Fabric

### Minecraft version

1.21.1

### Mod version

15.10.5

### Modloader version

fabricloader: Fabric Loader 0.18.4 fabric-api: 0.116.8+1.21.1

### Modpack info

_No response_

### [IMPORTANT] If bug:

- [ ] I have confirmed this bug is reproducible on a minimal setup, not a modpack with many other mods.

### [IMPORTANT] If bug: The **latest.log** file, not the crash report

_No response_

### Issue description

Hello,

I’m using Jade 15.10.5 (Fabric) on Minecraft 1.21.1, and I am encountering a crash related to Jade during certain runtime events.

The crash usually occurs when:

• Toggling shaders on/off (Iris)
• Player death and respawn
• Occasionally during **resource reload events

From the crash log, the exception appears to originate from Jade’s component registration:

java.lang.UnsupportedOperationException
at com.google.common.collect.ImmutableMultimap.put
at snownee.jade.impl.lookup.HierarchyLookup.register
at snownee.jade.impl.WailaClientRegistration.registerBlockComponent

This seems to happen while Jade plugins are being loaded or registered.

Example log snippet:

Caused by: java.lang.UnsupportedOperationException
at com.google.common.collect.ImmutableMultimap.put
at snownee.jade.impl.lookup.HierarchyLookup.register
at snownee.jade.impl.WailaClientRegistration.registerBlockComponent
at snownee.jade.impl.ClientRegistrationSession.end
at snownee.jade.util.CommonProxy.loadComplete

The crash happens right after Jade plugins initialize, including:

snownee.jade.addon.core.CorePlugin
net.blay09.mods.balm.fabric.compat.hudinfo.FabricJadeModCompat

The environment:

Minecraft: 1.21.1 (Fabric)
Fabric Loader: 

[latest.log](https://github.com/user-attachments/files/25941877/latest.log)

[latest.log](https://github.com/user-attachments/files/25941992/latest.log)

0.18.4
Java: OpenJDK 21

Some relevant mods in the environment:

• Sodium 0.6.0-beta.2
• Iris 1.8.1
• Distant Horizons 2.4.5-b
• Jade Addons 6.0.3
• EMI 1.1.22
• EMI Ores 1.2
• Fabric API 0.116.8

The crash most consistently happens when **shader state changes (Iris shader toggle) or when the **player respawns after death.

It appears that during those events a plugin attempts to register components into a structure backed by `ImmutableMultimap`, which then throws `UnsupportedOperationException`.

Could this be related to plugin registration happening after the registry becomes immutable, or during a resource reload phase where the lookup structure should no longer be modified?

If you need a full crash log or mod list, I can provide it.

Thank you for your work on Jade.

issues.body: ### Mod loader Forge ### Minecraft version 1.12-1.21.1 ### Mod version 15.1.0+ ### Modloader version Forge 47.3.22+ & NeoForge 21.1.215+ ### Modpack info _No response_ ### [IMPORTANT] If bug: - [ ] I have confirmed this bug is reproducible on a minimal setup, not a modpack with many other mods. ### [IMPORTANT] If bug: The **latest.log** file, not the crash report _No response_ ### Issue description Hello, this is more of a simple request: Im the author of the mod [Immersive Vehicles](https://www.curseforge.com/minecraft/mc-mods/minecraft-transport-simulator), and we had users report that the rendering entity that IV relies on is constantly being shown by jade. (Image below) The fix is quite simple, going into -> "config/jade/hide-entities.json" and pasting "`mts:builder_rendering`" into “`values`“:. The finalised code would look like this: ```json { "__comment": "This is a blocklist for the target of Jade. You can add registry ids to the \"values\" list. Restart the game to apply changes.", "values": [ "minecraft:area_effect_cloud", "minecraft:firework_rocket", "minecraft:interaction", "minecraft:text_display", "minecraft:lightning_bolt", "mts:builder_rendering" ] } ``` It would be great to have this be added to jades internal blacklist by default so people using the two mods together dont run into any more trouble. Thanks for reading, have a good one ;D

issues.title: [Suggestion] Add ability to disable tooltip for dropped items
issues.body:
### Mod loader

Fabric

### Minecraft version

1.20.1

### Mod version

11.13.1+fabric

### Modloader version

Fabric: Loader 0.18.2 + API 0.92.6+1.20.1

### Modpack info

_No response_

### [IMPORTANT] If bug:

- [ ] I have confirmed this bug is reproducible on a minimal setup, not a modpack with many other mods.

### [IMPORTANT] If bug: The **latest.log** file, not the crash report

_No response_

### Issue description

I noticed that there wasn't an option to disable Jade's tooltip for dropped items. I tried adding "minecraft:item" to the blocklist in "hide-entities.json", but Jade invalidated that file and reverted it to the default. So, I'd like to formerly suggest the ability to hide item tooltips through Jade.

issues.title: Undecapsulated `Optional` Type in RedstoneProvider.java
Width of `TextElementImpl` is miscalculated when Caxton is present
issues.body: ### Mod loader Fabric ### Minecraft version 1.21.11 ### Mod version 21.1.1 ### Modloader version Loader 0.18.2 + API 0.139.4+1.21.11 ### Modpack info _No response_ ### [IMPORTANT] If bug: - [x] I have confirmed this bug is reproducible on a minimal setup, not a modpack with many other mods. ### [IMPORTANT] If bug: The **latest.log** file, not the crash report https://gist.github.com/bluebear94/dd04c8b9f727c8efb69a783a86da3a85 ### Issue description When [Caxton](https://modrinth.com/mod/caxton/) 0.9.0-alpha.2+1.21.11-FABRIC is installed alongside Jade, the widths of `TextElementImpl` objects are miscalculated. This can result in the HUD tooltip appearing too wide: [Issue on Caxton’s repository.](https://gitlab.com/Kyarei/caxton/-/issues/102) I am reporting this both on Caxton’s repository and here because I’m not sure how to best fix this issue. ## Steps to reproduce 1. Start the game with Jade and Caxton and join a world 2. Enable the bundled Inter resource pack 3. Place a waxed weathered cut copper stairs block 4. Look at that block **Expected behavior:** The tooltip is just wide enough to fit the name of the block. **Actual behavior:** The tooltip is wider than the name of the block. ## Code analysis * Jade’s [`TextElementImpl`](https://github.com/Snownee/Jade/blob/26.1-fabric/src/main/java/snownee/jade/impl/ui/TextElementImpl.java#L28) calculates the width of a text according to `DisplayHelper.font()` * This returns an instance of `JadeFont` ([code](https://github.com/Snownee/Jade/blob/26.1-fabric/src/main/java/snownee/jade/overlay/DisplayHelper.java#L55)), which is a subclass of `Font` * Constructing a `Font` results in constructing a corresponding `StringSplitter` * When a `StringSplitter` is constructed, Caxton instantiates a corresponding `CaxtonTextHandler` (through [mixin injection](https://gitlab.com/Kyarei/caxton/-/blob/1.21.11/common/src/main/java/xyz/flirora/caxton/mixin/TextHandlerMixin.java?ref_type=heads#L38)), but at this time, the appropriate font set accessor is not yet known, so the CTH has a dummy accessor * `CaxtonTextHandler` needs a font set accessor (a `Function` derived from the font manager) instead of merely a `WidthProvider` because it requires complex text layout information from Caxton fonts. * When the `Font` is constructed, Caxton instantiates a `CaxtonTextRenderer` (again, through [mixin injection](https://gitlab.com/Kyarei/caxton/-/blob/1.21.11/common/src/main/java/xyz/flirora/caxton/mixin/TextRendererMixin.java?ref_type=heads#L46)), which [creates the real `CaxtonTextHandler`](https://gitlab.com/Kyarei/caxton/-/blob/1.21.11/common/src/main/java/xyz/flirora/caxton/render/CaxtonTextRenderer.java?ref_type=heads#L63) (and thereby [associates it with the vanilla `StringSplitter` held by `Font`](https://gitlab.com/Kyarei/caxton/-/blob/1.21.11/common/src/main/java/xyz/flirora/caxton/layout/CaxtonTextHandler.java?ref_type=heads#L70)) * After the `Font` constructor finishes, the `JadeFont` constructor [sets the splitter to a new instance](https://github.com/Snownee/Jade/blob/26.1-fabric/src/main/java/snownee/jade/util/JadeFont.java#L11), which is left with a dummy font set accessor * As a result, when Jade tries to calculate the width of some text, it does so as if no fonts are loaded.

issues.title: Powder Snow camouflage hides critical hazard information even when player is already affected
issues.body:
### Mod loader

Fabric

### Minecraft version

1.21.10

### Mod version

Jade-1.21.9-Fabric-20.1.0.jar

### Modloader version

Fabric Loader 0.18.4 + Fabric API 0.138.4 (1.21.10)

### Modpack info

Not using a modpack (manual mod setup). Mod list available if needed.

### [IMPORTANT] If bug:

- [ ] I have confirmed this bug is reproducible on a minimal setup, not a modpack with many other mods.

### [IMPORTANT] If bug: The **latest.log** file, not the crash report

_No response_

### Issue description

### Context
Jade has a built-in "camouflage" system that intentionally hides the real identity of certain blocks
(e.g. infested blocks, brushable blocks) in order to avoid spoiling gameplay mechanics.

This makes perfect sense for blocks that are explicitly designed to visually deceive the player.

### Problem
`minecraft:powder_snow` is currently treated as a camouflaged block and is always shown as a Snow Block.
However, Powder Snow is not a “mimic” block in the same sense as infested or brushable blocks — it is primarily a hazard.

The issue is that the camouflage remains active even when the player is already inside the Powder Snow
and is being affected by its mechanics (freezing / suffocation).

At that point, hiding the real block identity no longer prevents spoilers — it removes useful contextual information
and can actively confuse the player.

### User experience example
In normal gameplay, players usually do not constantly watch the Jade tooltip.
They tend to check it reactively, when something unusual or dangerous is happening.

In the case of Powder Snow:
- The player falls into the block
- Starts freezing or suffocating
- Checks Jade to understand what is happening
- Jade still reports "Snow Block", which is misleading in that context

### Design comparison
A hypothetical "quicksand" block would reasonably appear as normal sand before interaction,
but once the player starts sinking, showing it as "Sand" would be unhelpful and misleading.

Powder Snow fits the same pattern: once the hazard is active, the real identity is no longer a spoiler.

```
### Current implementation
The camouflage is applied unconditionally in `JadeClient.builtInOverrides(...)`:
```java
else if (target.getBlock() == Blocks.POWDER_SNOW) {
    Block block = Blocks.SNOW_BLOCK;
    return builder.blockState(block.defaultBlockState()).build();
}
```


Suggested improvement

Keep the camouflage behavior for Powder Snow before interaction,
but disable it once the player is affected by the block.

Possible approaches:

- If the player is inside Powder Snow (camera / player AABB), show minecraft:powder_snow
- If freezing damage or powder snow effect is active, show minecraft:powder_snow
- Alternatively, remove Powder Snow from built-in camouflage entirely

This would preserve the anti-spoiler intent while improving clarity and safety during active hazards.

Environment

- Minecraft 1.21.10
- Fabric
- Jade 20.1.0 (Fabric)
- Citrus 1.2.1 (Show powder snow correctly)
- Jade Addons 6.0.3

### Issue description

.minecraft\config\jade\hide-entities.json:

```
  "values": [
    "immersive_portals:nether_portal_new"
  ]
```

The mod nether-variant loads correctly, and its registered objects function normally in-game. Minecraft’s own Identifier class explicitly allows hyphens (-) in namespaces, so this is a valid ID.

**Actual behavior:**
Jade rejects these IDs and logs IllegalArgumentException errors during ignore list loading.

issues.title: Causing lag with FallingTree mod
issues.body:
To display the progress of breaking a block on the Jade GUI, this mod gets the hardness of the block/finds how long with the given tool to break the block, just by looking at the block.

A number of mods that allow you to instantly break a large number of wood or ores have a setting to at least partially consider the added time to break the block based on the original block.

I.E. it may add 0.5 of the time to break for extra blocks, so if a tree is 10 logs tall it will be 1 + 9(0.5) times longer to break.

Jade calls for this to be calculated when targeting the given block with the correct tool.

This is not an issue for small little trees and veins but if there is a larger tree, lets say 100 logs, Jade will make the game shit itself as it keeps calculating/recalculating how much to progress the bar, especially if another tree sprouts up and the logs are touching, or another player or entity is adding more blocks for whatever reason.

### Issue description

There is a problem in `FluidView#readDefault` that makes the fluid show as `Air` for large amounts. See https://github.com/AztechMC/Modern-Industrialization/issues/1103. The issue is that `CommonProxy.getFluidName(fluidObject)` will call `toFluidStack(fluid)` which does a cast of the amount to an `int`, causing issues if the amount is bigger than an int. I would suggest for example to pass an amount of 1, the name usually not being dependent on the amount of the stack. Thank you!

issues.title: Jade cannot be built locally
issues.body:
### Mod loader

NeoForge

### Minecraft version

1.21.1

### Mod version

15.9.2

### Modloader version

n/a

### Modpack info

_No response_

### [IMPORTANT] If bug:

- [x] I have confirmed this bug is reproducible on a minimal setup, not a modpack with many other mods.

### [IMPORTANT] If bug: The **latest.log** file, not the crash report

_No response_

### Issue description

Jade fails to build locally due to the inclusion of these two arguments in the `gradle.properties` file: `-DsocksProxyHost=127.0.0.1 -DsocksProxyPort=1079`

This results in esoteric network errors, such as 
```
> Uncaught exception while processing replacement of dependency net.neoforged:neoforge using handler net.neoforged.gradle.common.extensions.dependency.replacement.Handler_Decorated@7b6d1f01: Failed to download the file from: https://piston-meta.mojang.com/mc/game/version_manifest.json to: C:\Users\Shadows\.gradle\caches\minecraft\.\launcher_metadata.json
```

This is endemic to all branches (which means many updates may be necessary for Jade to be buildable externally without a local proxy setup).

If possible, I would suggest moving these flags to a local `gradle.properties` in your gradle user home ([ref](https://docs.gradle.org/current/userguide/build_environment.html#sec:gradle_configuration_properties)) or using environment variables.

Custom Payload not bounds checking and handling gracefully. issues.title: The "Required Tool" Doesn't also use the `HarvestCheckEvent`
issues.body:
### Mod loader

NeoForge

### Minecraft version

1.21.x

### Mod version

15.1.6

### Modloader version

Neo 21.1.6

### Modpack info

_No response_

### [IMPORTANT] If bug:

- [X] I have confirmed this bug is reproducible on a minimal setup, not a modpack with many other mods.

### [IMPORTANT] If bug: The **latest.log** file, not the crash report

_No response_

### Issue description

Basically I wanted to add the ability for certain items to break certain blocks. In order to do this though, I can't use data components to set the ToolRules for items I don't own, as the only event we have to modify those components, plays before tags are read in for items.

The alternative way to handle this then, is to use a combination of events in Neo to change the breakspeed and the harvest check. Jade's only problem here is the checkmark vs cancel sign that shows on the tooltip when a block is set to have `toolRequired`.

An Example of something without required appears fine. The tier is correct.
![image](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/87528419-b5f6-4aac-b66f-838a305846ba)


However, when looking at something that requires a tool but uses the `HarvestCheckEvent` and would allow, it shows it is not correct which may mislead players
![image](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/3528aa83-418c-44ad-8e3b-2f5201a66b11)



## Suggested Idea

Have the tooltip when a tool is require just call the event given I think most of the data is already present.

This might be tangentially related to #432 Given that the checks for tiers may result in a similar check since Minecraft changed how their tags work for block break tiers.

issues.title: Targeting a multipart Entity can be inconsistent due to subparts being hit-detected
issues.body:
### Mod loader

Forge

### Minecraft version

1.20.1

### Mod version

11.7.1

### Modloader version

Forge 47.1.28

### Modpack info

_No response_

### If bug:

- [ ] Can you reproduce this issue with relevant mods only?

### If bug: The latest.log file

_No response_

### Issue description

`RayTracing#canBeTarget` does not ever filter out instances of Forge's `PartEntity`, so the hit result for a multipart entity may be one of its subparts, and thus not trigger the correct display info as it is not an instance of its parent entity. Even apart from Forge, targeting multipart entities such as the Ender Dragon may be inconsistent as it has `EnderDragonPart`s which can be hit-detected (this multipart system is already integrated with Forge's multipart API). These subparts use the same `EntityType` as their parent entity, so they cannot be filtered out via the client config either.

In my own Forge mod with Jade compat, I apply an Injection Mixin into `RayTracing#canBeTarget` for debugging purposes. I have it return false if the entity is an instance of `PartEntity`. This allows me to consistently look at my multipart entity without hit-detecting the sub-parts. 

Perhaps some way to allow mods to provide their own entity ray trace filters would be better than permanently blacklisting all instances of Forge's `PartEntity` or vanilla's `EnderDragonPart`. One could imagine a use-case where a mod's entity subpart implementation having its own display info is desired. But a built-in blacklist may be more desirable in most cases.

issues.title: [NeoForge 1.20.2] Crash when looking at non-pickable entity
issues.body:
### Mod loader

NeoForge

### Minecraft version

1.20.2

### Mod version

12.1.7

### Modloader version

20.2.21-beta

### Modpack info

_No response_

### If bug:

- [ ] Can you reproduce this issue with relevant mods only?

### If bug: The latest.log file

https://gist.github.com/RedstoneDubstep/9f7aac0136571574e709543368b59843

### Issue description

Whenever the player looks at an entity that has no pick block interaction defined (so you don't get an item when you use the "Pick Block" key on it), the client crashes. This includes, for example, all projectiles like Arrows and Fireballs as well as other players.

The relevant Jade code is in `EntityAccessorClientHandler#getIcon`, which uses the picked result of the looked-at entity to try to generate an icon. However, this code doesn't contain a check for whether the picked result doesn't exist (and the returned `ItemStack` is thus `null`), so the game crashes with a NullPointerException when `getItem()` is invoked on the null stack. 
(Note: This wasn't an issue in the Forge implementation of Jade, because in Forge, `IForgeEntity#getPickedResult` always returned an optionally empty ItemStack, which is no longer the case in NeoForge where `null`return values from that method can and will happen.)
PS: I was only able to reproduce this in a development environment because it's currently impossible to install NeoForge on PrismLauncher, but judging by the way the issue occurs I'm very sure that this crash also happens in a production environment.

### Issue description

I played with the tooltip disabled up until the very last point when the game crashed.
I was looking at a crafting table from the Visual Workbench mod. The moment I enabled the Jade Tooltip by pressing NUMPAD 1, the game crashed. [Here](https://gist.github.com/KxttyKxt/12c832544ea1ff78a73eda8c8b9da6a4) is the crash log, with the header, `Unexpected Error: java.lang.NullPointerException: Cannot read field "f_82470_" because "translate" is null`. All suspected tile entities produce this same crash when looking directly at them (so that Jade attempts to render them in a tooltip).

This issue did not used to happen. It started happening a few days ago. Since then, the issue has also occurred with chests, armor stands, and beds, but not always for those three.

I suspect it is an issue with the [Faithless resource pack](https://www.curseforge.com/minecraft/texture-packs/faithless/files/4332556) I have enabled in this modpack. 

There is a mod that--when combined with this resource pack--allows special entity and tile entity and block rendering; this mod is [[EMF] Entity Model Features](https://www.curseforge.com/minecraft/mc-mods/entity-model-features/files/4780256). However, this issue persists even after I disabled EMF.

issues.title: Furnaces don't show contents without an item in the input slot currently being smelted
issues.body: ### Mod loader Forge ### Minecraft version 1.19.2 ### Mod version 8.8.1 (Forge) / 8.7.3 (Fabric) ### Modloader version Forge: 43.2.0 / Fabric Loader 0.14.21 + Fabric API 0.76.0 ### Modpack info n/a ### If bug: - [X] Can you reproduce this issue with relevant mods only? ### If bug: The latest.log file https://gist.github.com/unilock/e12f78af070832be94abc2c2a3fc9113 ### Issue description With the "Item Storage" config option enabled, a furnace (or blast furnace, smoker, etc.) will not show its contents unless it both has an item in its input slot, and is currently smelting that item. For example: - A furnace with no items will not show its contents (as expected). ✅ - A furnace with cobblestone in the input slot, sticks in the fuel slot, and nothing in the output slot will show its contents. ✅ - A furnace with only cobblestone in the input slot + an empty fuel slot, but still smelting that cobblestone with burn time left over from the last fuel item consumed, will show its contents. ✅ - A furnace with an item in the output slot will not show its contents, regardless of whether an item is in the fuel slot / how much burn time is left. ❌ - A furnace with only an item in the fuel slot will not show its contents, regardless of how much burn time is left. ❌ The desired behavior would be that furnace contents are *always* displayed, so I don't have to check every one of my wall of 45 furnaces to see which one I put my 5 raw iron in :v

### Issue description

## Problem

## Replication steps

1. Place a chest
2. Fill 999 items in the chest, Inventory preview will show the correct count "999x Stone"

issues.title: [1.19.x] ObjectDataCenter inaccessible from api
issues.body:
### Mod loader

Fabric

### Minecraft version

1.19.x

### Mod version

8.6.4+

### Modloader version

Forge 43.0.0 / Fabric 0.58.6+1.19.2 (any version, really)

### Modpack info

_No response_

### If bug:

- [ ] Can you reproduce this issue with relevant mods only?

### If bug: The latest.log file

_No response_

### Issue description

I run into the following problem when implementing a cutom JadeRayTraceCallback: I want return a block/entitiy at a diffrerent position and therefor have to retrun a new/modified accessor instance. The problem is because i want to return an acessor for a different position, the original acessor passed to the callback might be null (in case of a miss). When that happes, i cannot access the serverData and serverConnected properties. Instead i would have to use the ObjectDataCenter. The problem with that is, that it cannot be accessed from just the api, as its only available in the implentation of jade. Why would i want to rely only on the api? Because i am using a multiloader setup (common project and two subprojects [forge and fabric]) and do want to duplicate code. A workaround for this would be a serviceloader, but i think it should be considered that the serverData and serverConnected properties can be accessed via the api.

issues.title: [feature] Do not disable Jade when player list is enabled
issues.body:
### Mod loader

Fabric

### Minecraft version

1.19.2

### Mod version

8.2.1

### Modloader version

Fabric Loader 0.14.10


## Problem

Sometimes, the player list contains info that is relevant at all times. For example, when using Carpet `/log tps`, the player list contains some useful info about server performance. It then makes sense to use Tweakeroo `AlwaysDisplayPlayerList` (for example) to track this useful info by having the player list always display. 

However, Jade disables itself when the player list is active. While that is normally useful, as Jade default position and the player list conflict, one can reposition the Jade display so that it does not conflict, henceforth enjoying both the Jade display and the player list display. 

There is a setting to not disable Jade rendering when other screens are open, but that makes Jade also overlay itself on top of the F3 screen and other screens where it is actually annoying to have it. 

## Solution

Have a separate toggle config to control if Jade should show itself when the player list is active;
Default is Jade OFF so that default behavior remains unchanged from prior Jade versions.

issues.body:
### Mod loader

Fabric

### Minecraft version

1.19

### Mod version

7.3.1

### Modloader version

 Fabric Loader 0.14.6, API 0.55.1+1.19

### Modpack info

_No response_

### Issue description

## Feature Request: support for double chests

When looking at a double chest, the tooltip presents the content of the targeted half of the double chest. This is annoying as many chest halls are based on having double chests with a side facing the user (thus the 'back' chest is not immediately targetable). 

## Subfeatures

### Summarize identical elements

When a chest contains multiple stacks of the same item (or only one type of item), the content is presented as [item1]x64 [item1]x64 [item2]x16, etc.

This could be simplified to [item1]x128 [item2]x16, ordered by quantity. 

### Summarize number of stacks

This is a followup of the previous idea: show [item1]x128 (2 stacks) [item2]x16 [item3]x96 (1.5 stacks)
Note how 'item2' doesn't have a stack count as it is less (or equal) to 1 stack.

As the related error info is pretty short , I will paste it directly into it. The full log is ready to upload if needed.

Waystones version: forge-1.18.2-10.0.0

This is how the WAILA plugin is implemented in Waystones mod.
https://github.com/ModdingForBlockheads/Waystones/blob/1f425a2d2e882b4a81615d4115410c7559a76f34/forge/src/main/java/net/blay09/mods/waystones/compat/WailaProvider.java#L18-L47

It looks like the API refactoring is probably the cause of this incompatibility. Mods developed for both forge and fabric may still follow the old API conventions as the fabric fork is still using the old ones.

issues.title: [1.16.5] Block Name Format Error
issues.body:
* Forge Version: 36.1.24
 * Mod Version: 1.16.4-2.7.2
 * Can you reproduce this issue with relevant mods only?: yes

When looking at a block which name has parameters, Jade will show "Format error" while The One Probe will show correctly.
![2021-07-21_17 46 35](https://user-images.githubusercontent.com/20498895/126469431-7801c25b-6613-40f4-a2be-2dbe57bcabbd.png)
The reason is that Jade uses the `I18n.format` method to get the block name directly.
https://github.com/Snownee/Jade/blob/39c9eb453b12753348e1caa101d39875ee9c6d1e/src/main/java/mcp/mobius/waila/addons/core/BaseBlockProvider.java#L63-L65
However, The One Probe gets the block as an ItemStack first, and then gets the name of the ItemStack.
https://github.com/McJtyMods/TheOneProbe/blob/148f5013fb01a7eceea5bbd625fe8f9bb605775a/src/main/java/mcjty/theoneprobe/apiimpl/providers/DefaultProbeInfoProvider.java#L383-L390

* Minecraft Version: 1.16.4+

Hope you consider. Thanks for your time!
